scenes.visual: Title card: Hubs That Compete.

scenes.tts: Once a few genes slip out of the silence, how does just one of them win?
scenes.visual: Three faintly glowing receptor genes in a grey nucleus, each with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Once a few genes slip out of the silence, how does just one of them win?

scenes.tts: An enhancer is a stretch of DNA that raises transcription of a gene it contacts.
scenes.visual: A DNA loop brings a small green element up against a gene, which brightens. Label: enhancer.
scenes.narration: An enhancer is a stretch of DNA that raises transcription of a gene it contacts.

scenes.tts: The receptor genes have candidate enhancers, which the field calls the Greek Islands.
scenes.visual: Small green islands dotted across several chromosomes. Label: the Greek Islands.
scenes.narration: The receptor genes have candidate enhancers, which the field calls the Greek Islands.

scenes.tts: Contacts in trans are contacts between different chromosomes.
scenes.visual: Two differently coloured chromosomes touch at one point. Label: in trans = between chromosomes.
scenes.narration: Contacts in trans are contacts between different chromosomes.

scenes.tts: A hub is a cluster of enhancers, often from different chromosomes. An active hub sits around the gene it drives.
scenes.visual: Green islands from three chromosomes cluster around one receptor gene, which glows. Label: active hub.
scenes.narration: A hub is a cluster of enhancers, often from different chromosomes. An active hub sits around the gene it drives.

scenes.tts: Markenscoff-Papadimitriou and colleagues linked receptor transcription to contacts between enhancers on different chromosomes.
scenes.visual: Fluorescent dots for an enhancer and a receptor gene sit close together in one nucleus. Label: Markenscoff-Papadimitriou and colleagues, 2014.
scenes.narration: Markenscoff-Papadimitriou and colleagues linked receptor transcription to contacts between enhancers on different chromosomes.

scenes.tts: A chromatin remodeler, B P T F, helped make those contacts.
scenes.caption: A chromatin remodeler, Bptf, helped make those contacts.
scenes.visual: A remodeling protein labelled Bptf nudges the chromosomes together.
scenes.narration: A chromatin remodeler, Bptf, helped make those contacts.

scenes.tts: Disrupting the contacts was linked to weak expression of several receptors at once.
scenes.visual: The hub breaks apart; three receptor genes glow dimly at the same time.
scenes.narration: Disrupting the contacts was linked to weak expression of several receptors at once.

scenes.tts: What builds the hubs? Two transcription factors, L H X two and E B F, bind cooperatively at enhancer motifs with a set spacing.
scenes.caption: What builds the hubs? Two transcription factors, Lhx2 and Ebf, bind cooperatively at enhancer motifs with a set spacing.
scenes.visual: Two protein shapes, Lhx2 and Ebf, dock side by side on a green island at a fixed distance apart.
scenes.narration: What builds the hubs? Two transcription factors, Lhx2 and Ebf, bind cooperatively at enhancer motifs with a set spacing.

scenes.tts: Nearly every E B F site in the receptor clusters was also bound by L H X two.
scenes.caption: Nearly every Ebf site in the receptor clusters was also bound by Lhx2.
scenes.visual: A Venn diagram: the Ebf circle sits almost entirely inside the Lhx2 circle. On screen: 63 of 65 Ebf peaks.
scenes.narration: Nearly every Ebf site in the receptor clusters was also bound by Lhx2.

scenes.tts: An inserted array of enhancer elements raised how often linked receptors were chosen. That is a sufficiency-style test.
scenes.visual: A row of extra green islands is added beside a receptor gene; that gene lights up in more neurons.
scenes.narration: An inserted array of enhancer elements raised how often linked receptors were chosen. That is a sufficiency-style test.

scenes.tts: Monahan, Horta and Lomvardas then extended the contact maps across the whole genome.
scenes.visual: A genome-wide contact heat map assembles square by square. Label: in situ Hi-C, 2019.
scenes.narration: Monahan, Horta and Lomvardas then extended the contact maps across the whole genome.

scenes.tts: Receptor clusters on eighteen chromosomes contacted one another.
scenes.caption: Receptor clusters on 18 chromosomes contacted one another.
scenes.visual: Eighteen chromosomes, each with a receptor cluster marked, linked by contact lines.
scenes.narration: Receptor clusters on 18 chromosomes contacted one another.

scenes.tts: The factors L H X two and L D B one regulated how these hubs assemble and are maintained.
scenes.caption: The factors LHX2 and LDB1 regulated how these hubs assemble and are maintained.
scenes.visual: Lhx2 and Ldb1 pieces snap into a hub, holding it together.
scenes.narration: The factors LHX2 and LDB1 regulated how these hubs assemble and are maintained.

scenes.tts: But a contact map from many cells is an average. It cannot show that each cell has a single hub.
scenes.visual: The heat map splits into thousands of faint cell outlines behind it. Caution label: population average.
scenes.narration: But a contact map from many cells is an average. It cannot show that each cell has a single hub.

scenes.tts: So look inside one developing neuron. Is there one hub, or several?
scenes.visual: Zoom into a single immature neuron's nucleus. Question mark.
scenes.narration: So look inside one developing neuron. Is there one hub, or several?

scenes.tts: Several, before one gene wins. Pourmorady and colleagues inferred competing hubs in single developing neurons.
scenes.visual: Two or three hubs light up at once in the nucleus, each around a different receptor gene. Label: Pourmorady and colleagues, 2024.
scenes.narration: Several, before one gene wins. Pourmorady and colleagues inferred competing hubs in single developing neurons.

scenes.tts: They combined single-cell readouts of RNA and open chromatin with single-cell contact maps.
scenes.visual: Two panels: in multiome cells, RNA and chromatin accessibility are read together; in a separate set of nuclei, Dip-C gives contact maps. Arrows from both feed one shared model.
scenes.narration: They combined single-cell readouts of RNA and open chromatin with single-cell contact maps.

scenes.tts: Their evidence supported two further steps. First, receptor RNA suppressed transcription of competing receptors at a distance.
scenes.visual: One hub brightens; RNA from its gene spreads out, and the rival hubs dim.
scenes.narration: Their evidence supported two further steps. First, receptor RNA suppressed transcription of competing receptors at a distance.

scenes.tts: The machinery behind that long-range suppression is still unidentified.
scenes.visual: A dotted question-mark shape sits between the RNA and the dimming rivals.
scenes.narration: The machinery behind that long-range suppression is still unidentified.

scenes.tts: Second, translation of the receptor then stabilized transcription at the winning hub.
scenes.visual: Receptor protein appears outside the nucleus; the winning hub locks bright.
scenes.narration: Second, translation of the receptor then stabilized transcription at the winning hub.

scenes.tts: So competition can work without receptor protein, and protein then helps stabilize the winner. One receptor per neuron is the endpoint.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: hubs compete; the winner's RNA quiets rivals; protein stabilizes; one receptor is the endpoint, not every stage.
scenes.narration: So competition can work without receptor protein, and protein then helps stabilize the winner. One receptor per neuron is the endpoint.

scenes.visual: End card: Hubs That Compete.
